claims.claim: Jimmy Wales and Larry Sanger launched Wikipedia on 15 January 2001.
claims.episode_span: Jimmy Wales and Larry Sanger launched Wikipedia on 15 January 2001 as a volunteer-written encyclopedia
claims.supporting_quote: In 2001, the license for Nupedia was changed to GFDL , and Jimmy Wales and Larry Sanger launched Wikipedia as a complementary project, using an online wiki as a collaborative drafting tool.

claims.claim: The English Wikipedia reached one million articles in 2006 (its one-millionth article was created on March 1, 2006).
claims.episode_span: The English Wikipedia grew from a few hundred articles in 2001 to more than one million by 2006
claims.supporting_quote: The English Wikipedia gained its one-millionth article, Jordanhill railway station , on March 1, 2006.

claims.claim: A 2005 peer review by the journal Nature of 42 science entries found few differences in accuracy between Wikipedia and Encyclopaedia Britannica.
claims.episode_span: a 2005 Nature study comparing Wikipedia favorably to Encyclopædia Britannica further validated the model
claims.supporting_quote: a peer review in 2005 of forty-two scientific entries on both Wikipedia and Encyclopædia Britannica by the science journal Nature found few differences in accuracy

claims.claim: Estimates placed women at only 8.5-15 percent of active Wikipedia contributors in 2011, with a 2013 peer-reviewed study estimating 16.1 percent.
claims.episode_span: A 2011 follow-up study estimated that only 8.5 to 16 percent of editors were women
claims.supporting_quote: making up only 8.5–15% of active contributors in 2011. [ 4 ] [ 5 ] A peer-reviewed study published in 2013 estimated 16.1% of editors were women.

claims.claim: WikiProject Women in Red launched on English Wikipedia in the summer of 2015, focused on creating articles about notable women.
claims.episode_span: community initiatives such as WikiProject Women in Red
claims.supporting_quote: In the summer of 2015, the WikiProject Women in Red was launched on the English-language version of Wikipedia, focusing on the creation of new articles about notable women.
